name: gradient
summary: A living background of four soft color blobs or of aurora curtains, mixed in OKLab, without banding, with a light film grain.
looks: Four soft blobs of color drift slowly over the element on looping paths that take minutes to repeat, their edges bent by noise. They lean toward the pointer and shift as the page scrolls. Colors mix in OKLab, so two colors meet through a clean middle instead of a muddy gray, and every pixel is dithered, so smooth ramps show no bands. A light film grain sits on top; set grain to 0 for a clean gradient or around 0.08 for a film look. The aurora style draws the first color as a night sky and the other three as curtains of light that wave along it, sharp at their lower edge and rising in uneven rays.
target: an empty decorative element behind the content, such as an aria-hidden div filling a hero; its CSS background is the look without WebGL

params.name: style
params.description: mesh drifts four soft blobs into a wash of color, for most heroes and sections; aurora draws the first color as a dark sky with the other three as waving curtains of light, for a night or tech hero over a dark page.

params.name: color1
params.description: Color of the first blob, any CSS color; with aurora, the sky.

params.name: color2
params.description: Color of the second blob; with aurora, the first curtain.

params.name: color3
params.description: Color of the third blob; with aurora, the second curtain.

params.name: color4
params.description: Color of the fourth blob; with aurora, the third curtain.

params.name: speed
params.description: How fast the blobs travel along their paths.

params.name: scale
params.description: Size of the blobs: below 1 sharper patches, above 1 softer washes.

params.name: warp
params.description: How much noise bends the blobs’ edges.

params.name: attract
params.description: How far the blobs lean toward the pointer while it is over the element.

params.name: scroll
params.description: How far the blobs move along their paths while the element crosses the viewport.

params.name: grain
params.description: Strength of the film grain, one CSS pixel per grain; 0 leaves only the dithering.

params.name: fps
params.description: Most frames a second the drift draws; 0 holds it still.

params.name: octaves
params.description: Layers of noise in the warp, 1 to 3.

params.name: seed
params.description: Paths of the blobs and shape of the noise.

frames.note: Up to fps frames a second while on screen, none off screen or at fps 0; pointer and scroll draw at full rate. The grain changes with those frames and adds none.

reducedMotion.note: A still gradient: the blobs and the grain stop, and neither the pointer nor scroll moves them.

touch: The blobs lean toward a finger while it is on the screen; scrolling works as usual.

notes.low: At most 15 frames a second, one layer of noise in the warp.

cost.gpu: One pass over the element: one to three reads of a small noise tile, four exponentials and a hash per pixel.
cost.memory: A 64 × 64 noise tile shared by every gradient on the page.

name: dots
summary: A dot grid behind a hero or in a card that answers the pointer: dots near it grow, move aside or glow, then settle back.
looks: An even grid of small dots, plus marks or squares, the same pattern a CSS radial-gradient background draws. Around the pointer a soft lens forms: marks grow and take the accent color, slide away from it, or light up with a halo, depending on the mode. When the pointer stops the lens settles on it, and when it leaves the grid eases back. Drift slides the whole grid slowly, and fade lets it dissolve toward the edges. The background color of the element, read when the effect starts, stays under the grid.
target: an empty decorative element behind the content, such as an aria-hidden div filling a hero or the top of a card; a CSS dot pattern on it is the look without WebGL

params.name: style
params.description: dots draws round dots; plus draws thin plus marks, four times as wide as dot; squares draws small squares.

params.name: mode
params.description: grow enlarges and tints marks near the pointer; push moves them aside; glow tints them with a halo.

params.name: gap
params.description: Distance between mark centers in CSS pixels.

params.name: dot
params.description: Mark size in CSS pixels: a dot's diameter or a square's side; a plus is 4 times wider.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the marks at rest, any CSS color.

params.name: accent
params.description: Color marks take under the pointer, any CSS color.

params.name: radius
params.description: Reach of the pointer lens in CSS pixels; 0 turns the pointer off.

params.name: strength
params.description: Strength of the lens: how much marks grow, move or glow; 0 turns it off.

params.name: speed
params.description: Speed at which the grid slides; 0 keeps it in place.

params.name: fade
params.description: How far the grid fades out toward the edges, from none to the middle.

frames.note: Frames only while the pointer moves over the grid and for about a second while the lens settles; with speed, up to 30 frames a second while on screen.

reducedMotion.note: A still grid: no slide and no lens.

touch: No lens on touch screens, so a finger never draws frames; the slide still runs and scrolling works as usual.

notes.low: No slide: the grid moves only under the pointer.

cost.gpu: One pass over the element with a little math per pixel; push draws the nine nearest marks per pixel.

name: waves
summary: Topographic contour lines or flowing wave lines across a hero or footer, slowly changing and shifted by scroll.
looks: Thin lines in one color over a flat background. The contour style draws the lines of a topographic map over a relief that slowly changes shape, with every fifth line a little bolder like the index lines of a real map. The waves style draws lines that run across the element and flow sideways in soft swells, and stripes fills every other band between them. Lines keep the same width in CSS pixels wherever they run, and where they crowd together they blend into an even tone instead of flickering.
target: an empty decorative element behind the content, such as an aria-hidden div filling a hero or a footer; its CSS background is the look without WebGL

params.name: style
params.description: contour draws the lines of a topographic map over a slowly changing relief; waves draws lines flowing across the element; stripes fills every other band between those lines.

params.description: Color of the lines or stripes, any CSS color.

params.name: background

params.name: warp

params.name: speed
params.description: How fast the relief and the swells change; 0 keeps their shape.

params.name: thickness
params.description: Line width in CSS pixels; stripes ignore it.

params.name: scroll
params.description: How far the lines move while the element crosses the viewport.

params.name: fps
params.description: Most frames a second the motion draws; 0 holds it still.

params.name: seed
params.description: Shape of the noise that bends the lines.

frames.note: Up to fps frames a second while on screen, none off screen or at fps 0; scroll draws at full rate.

reducedMotion.note: A still frame: the lines neither change nor move with scroll.

touch: Nothing changes on touch screens: scroll moves the lines as usual.

cost.gpu: One pass over the element: four or eight reads of a small noise tile per pixel.
cost.memory: A 128 × 128 noise tile in half floats per element, 128 KB.

name: stars
summary: A night sky of twinkling stars in depth layers that lean with the pointer and the scroll, with shooting stars and a warp flight.
looks: Hundreds of small stars over a flat sky color, most faint and a few bright, some warmer and some cooler. They twinkle, drift slowly sideways, nearer ones faster, and lean with the pointer and the scroll, so the sky has depth. A fast scroll stretches them into vertical streaks, and now and then a shooting star crosses the upper sky and fades. The warp motion flies through the field instead: stars rush out from the center and stretch into trails.
target: an empty decorative element behind the content, such as an aria-hidden div filling a hero; its CSS background is the look without WebGL

params.description: drift twinkles and drifts slowly; warp flies through the stars; still keeps them in place.

params.description: How far a fast scroll stretches the stars into streaks; 0 never stretches.

params.name: scale
params.description: Size of the stars over a base of about 1 px.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the stars, any CSS color; each star tints it slightly.

params.name: background
params.description: Color of the sky behind the stars, any CSS color.

params.name: shooting
params.description: Shooting stars a minute on average; 0 turns them off.

params.name: fps
params.description: Most frames a second the motion draws; 0 holds the stars still.

params.name: seed
params.description: Positions, sizes and colors of the stars.

frames.note: Up to fps frames a second while on screen, none off screen, at fps 0 or with the still motion; pointer and scroll draw at full rate.

reducedMotion.note: A still sky: no twinkle, drift, warp, shooting stars, parallax or streaks, and no frames.

touch: The stars lean with a finger while it is on the screen; scroll parallax and streaks work as usual.

notes.low: At most 300 stars and 24 frames a second.

cost.gpu: One pass for the sky and one instanced draw of small quads for all the stars.
cost.memory: Two instance buffers of 4003 entries, about 128 KB.

name: blobs
summary: Soft blobs of brand color drifting behind a hero: merging like a lava lamp, as blurred orbs or as glossy glass drops.
looks: Up to eight round blobs in four brand colors float slowly over a flat background on looping paths, each swelling and shrinking a little on its own rhythm. In the lava style they merge where they meet and pull apart again, with soft edges and colors that blend in OKLab where two blobs join. Orbs keeps them apart as blurred discs layered over each other, the look behind frosted glass cards. Glass shades the merged shapes as glossy drops with a highlight and a bright rim, the background showing through their middle. They lean toward the pointer and move along their paths as the page scrolls. Unlike gradient, which fills the whole box with one wash of color, blobs keeps distinct shapes with the background between them.

name: clouds
summary: A sky of soft layered clouds for the time of day, daylight, a sunset or a moonlit night, drifting in the wind and parting on scroll.
looks: A sky gradient from the horizon up with up to three layers of clouds over it. Clouds shrink and thin out toward the horizon, so the sky has depth; each one is lit from the sun, bright on its sunny side, darker where it is thick and underneath, with a glowing edge where it is thin. The wind moves the layers sideways, nearer ones faster, and the scroll and the pointer shift them apart. The day style has a blue sky with white clouds and a pale sun high up, sunset an orange to violet sky with peach clouds and the sun low, night a dark blue sky with stars and clouds lit by the moon.
target: an empty decorative element behind the content, such as an aria-hidden div filling a hero; its CSS background is the look without WebGL

name: grid
summary: A grid floor in perspective running toward the viewer under a glowing horizon: neon synthwave, a blueprint or plain thin lines.
looks: The lower part of the element is a floor of square cells seen from just above, its lines running toward the viewer and meeting at the horizon. The upper part is the sky. Neon draws bright lines with a soft halo over a dark floor, the sky warming to the accent color at the horizon and a sun with bands cut through its lower half. Blueprint draws pale lines on a blue paper color with every fifth line heavier and the sun as a drawn circle. Minimal draws thin lines that fade out toward the horizon over a flat color, with the sun as a flat disc. Lines keep their width in CSS pixels and blend into an even tone where they crowd near the horizon, so the floor never shimmers. The pointer turns the view a little and the scroll moves the floor forward.
target: an empty decorative element behind the content, such as an aria-hidden div filling a hero; its CSS background is the look without WebGL

params.description: neon, glowing lines and a striped sun, for gaming, music events and synthwave looks; blueprint, pale lines on blue paper with heavier major lines, for engineering, hardware and developer tools; minimal, thin lines fading into a flat color, for calm tech and SaaS pages.
